title: Marguerite and the Veil
premise: Jude Pemberton, an exiled storm-caller keeping ledgers for the Guild of Impossible Things, discovers that the guild's oldest debt is owed by King Aldric — whose crown is a parasite called the Veil, feeding on his memories to hold the border wards together. When the wards collapse and the stars go out, Jude and their found family of guild misfits must trace the debt through thirteen turns of the moon, gathering the scattered pieces of Aldric's stolen past. Unbinding the king means choosing between restoring a lawful order built on one man's erasure and forging justice outside the law. In the end, Jude calls down the storm they were exiled for, shattering the Veil and letting the guild's ledger — not the crown — become the kingdom's memory.
about_author: I. M. Reyes is the pen name of a former archivist who claims to have catalogued three impossible objects and lost only one. They write fantasy about people who keep records of things the world would rather forget.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A quiet night at the Guild of Impossible Things: Jude balances accounts of traded shadows and bottled lullabies while bantering with the found family around them — forger Sable, retired knight Oren, and child medium Pip. The beat is warmth and routine, undercut when every entry in the ledger older than fifty years fades to blank paper at midnight.

chapters.title: Thirteen Turns
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The border wards fall with a sound like breaking glass; the stars go out one constellation at a time. The guild masters reveal a sealed page: King Aldric owes the guild an unpaid debt from before his coronation. The beat is dread and reluctant duty as the family realizes the debt is the key to everything vanishing.

chapters.title: What Wore the Crown
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Smuggled into the capital as debt-collectors, they glimpse the king through a warding glass: a hollow man with something vast and patient wearing him like a glove. Pip touches the palace gates and hears a child crying inside the king's head. The beat is horror tempered by compassion — the enemy may also be a victim.

chapters.title: A Debt in Ash
chapters.summary: Oren's POV. The trail leads to a burned monastery where young Aldric once bargained away his memories to save his dying kingdom. Oren, who served the crown and was discarded, confronts his old shame among the ashes. They recover the first memory-shard: a boy promising 'anything' to a voice in a well. The beat is grief turning to resolve.

chapters.title: The Guild of Forgotten Names
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. Seeking allies, the family finds a splinter guild of people erased by the Veil — citizens whose names no longer appear in any record. Their leader, a woman with no face, offers help at a price: Jude must surrender their exile story, the last proof of who they were. The beat is belonging versus identity.

chapters.title: Storm-Caller, Called to Account
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The price is paid, and Jude's exile is revealed: they once called a storm to drown a corrupt magistrate's court, killing innocents alongside the guilty. The found family absorbs this without flinching, but Jude wavers, doubting their right to judge the Veil. The beat is confession met with grace.

chapters.title: The Moon's Twelfth Turn
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Racing the penultimate moonrise, they steal two more shards from the royal vault using Sable's finest forgery — a fake decree commanding the Veil itself. It works too well: the Veil notices them, and Oren is taken into the palace as bait. The beat is triumph curdling into trap.

chapters.title: Inside the Hollow King
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. Pip walks into the king's dreams to reach Oren, navigating Aldric's shredded childhood — birthdays, betrayals, the well-voice's first whisper. Pip finds Oren caged in memory and learns the Veil's weakness: it cannot hold a memory freely given back. The beat is courage in a landscape of sorrow.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Turn
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Climax. On the final moonless night, the family storms the throne room. Jude chooses not to destroy the Veil but to out-ledger it: they read aloud every recovered memory, giving each one back to Aldric until the parasite starves. When it lashes out, Jude calls the storm they swore never to call again — precise, merciful, and final.

chapters.title: Ledgers and Lanterns
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Resolution. The stars return; the kingdom rebuilds its records from the guild's books, justice administered by consent rather than crown. Aldric, restored and diminished, abdicates to a council. Jude stays with the family that chose them, opening a fresh ledger whose first entry reads: 'Everything remembered, nothing owed.' The beat is hard-won peace.
